gloss: to show frustration; to be visibly upset (about a loss or failure)

definitions.gloss: to show frustration; to be visibly upset; to express vexation
definitions.explanation: To outwardly display feelings of frustration, regret, or bitterness, especially after a loss or missed opportunity. Formed from {悔|くや}しい (frustrating) + the suffix ～がる (to show signs of).

examples.english: They were visibly frustrated at losing.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{悔|くや}しがって{泣|な}いている。
examples.english: The child is crying out of frustration.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けた{選手|せんしゅ}が{悔|くや}しがる{姿|すがた}に{胸|むね}を{打|う}たれた。
examples.english: I was moved by the sight of the player showing frustration after the loss.

notes:
Formed from {悔|くや}しい (frustrating, vexing) + the suffix ～がる, which converts an adjective describing internal feelings into a verb describing the outward display of those feelings.

THE ～がる PATTERN:
Japanese い-adjectives describing emotions (like {悔|くや}しい, {嬉|うれ}しい, {怖|こわ}い) directly describe the speaker's own feelings. To describe someone else showing those feelings, add ～がる:
- {悔|くや}しい → {悔|くや}しがる: to show frustration
- {嬉|うれ}しい → {嬉|うれ}しがる: to show happiness
- {怖|こわ}い → {怖|こわ}がる: to show fear
- {寂|さび}しい → {寂|さび}しがる: to show loneliness

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {負|ま}けて{悔|くや}しがる: to be frustrated at losing
- ひどく{悔|くや}しがる: to be deeply frustrated
- {悔|くや}しがる{様子|ようす}: a frustrated demeanor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悔|くや}しい: frustrating — the base adjective describing the feeling itself
- {悔|く}やむ: to regret — focuses on remorse over a past action
- {残念|ざんねん}がる: to express disappointment — milder and less bitter
